solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Scratch a piece of bed linen — match results shown here?

parts.note: to scratch or score is to mark a surface with a line
a sheet is a piece of bed linen

explanation.surface: A housekeeper marks a bedsheet, oddly wondering whether the football results are recorded on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A record card of a game's points is where the final tally of a match is written down.

clue.text: Dogs one brought into film festival location

indicators.note: the single letter for 'one' is placed inside the town's name

parts.note: Cannes on the French Riviera hosts the famous film festival
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone brings a dog to the red carpet at a film festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Canine is the zoological term for a member of the dog family, so the plural means dogs.

clue.text: Spoiled pear harvest

indicators.note: something spoiled is damaged, so the letters of the fruit are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grower laments a crop of pears gone bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to harvest a crop is to gather or cut it in.

clue.text: Alcoholic drink from the woman beginning to renationalise railway

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a woman

indicators.note: the start of the word renationalise supplies its opening letter

explanation.surface: A political-sounding tale of a woman campaigning to bring the railways back into public ownership.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a fortified Spanish wine from Jerez is a classic aperitif.

clue.text: Spaces for printers: City editor keeps five in servitude

parts.note: an en is a printer's unit of spacing, so the plural gives several of them

indicators.note: the city and editor hold the numeral between them

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles, the crossword's favourite city
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A newspaper's City editor is accused of keeping five typesetters toiling like slaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City editor' reads as one newspaper job title, the City desk covering finance, but the two words split into separate pieces that hold the numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone held in servitude has been made a slave.

clue.text: Bitter harangue cutting off Di and a close-knit group

indicators.note: the name and the article are removed from the start of the longer word

parts.note: a diatribe is a bitter verbal attack
taken as written, a short form of Diana

explanation.surface: A furious rant leads to Di being shut out of her tight circle of friends.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribe is a closely bound social group, such as a clan or extended family.

clue.text: Landlord boss's pre-printed stationery

parts.note: one who lets property is, whimsically, a letter
a head is a boss, with the apostrophe s read as the possessive joining the pieces

explanation.surface: The landlord's boss has smart headed notepaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Landlord' is crossword wit: someone who lets a property is a 'letter'.
explanation.definitionFit: Headed notepaper carries a printed name and address at the top before anything is written.

clue.text: Vote against closure of Electric Avenue, curving inwards

parts.note: con is a vote or argument against, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: the closing letter of the word Electric is taken

explanation.surface: Residents vote against shutting Electric Avenue, a street that bends round.
explanation.walkthrough: Electric Avenue is a real street in Brixton, south London, which adds to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A surface that is hollowed like the inside of a bowl bends inwards.

clue.text: Colonel associated with us, not so neutral or tame?

parts.note: COL is the military abbreviation for colonel
our means belonging to or connected with us
less means to a smaller degree, not so much

explanation.surface: A colonel admits that people like us are rather bland and unadventurous.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking hue makes a thing neutral, and figuratively dull or insipid, hence tame.

clue.text: Show some flashiness?

indicators.note: only some of the letters of flashiness are wanted, a run inside it

explanation.surface: A question asking whether flamboyance is just a bit of display.
explanation.definitionFit: To be outstanding or excel is to stand out, to show well, as in 'she'll come into her own'.

clue.text: Kiln's broken connection

indicators.note: a broken kiln falls apart, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A potter laments that the kiln is damaged.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Kiln's stands for 'is', a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a tie or bond between two things, like one ring in a chain.

clue.text: Other ranks nominate every other part of unit for decoration

parts.note: OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
to nominate someone is to name them

indicators.note: alternate letters of the word unit are taken

explanation.surface: Soldiers below officer rank put forward someone from the unit for a medal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Every other part of unit' takes the second and fourth letters, NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an adornment or trinket added purely for decoration.

clue.text: Unwilling to work with British on Muslim festival, the French

parts.note: Eid is the festival marking the end of Ramadan or of the pilgrimage
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: A British worker skips work during a Muslim holiday spent in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: utterly lazy, idle to the very bones.

clue.text: Result of photo of the sky?

parts.note: up is where the sky is, so a picture of it points up
a shot is a photograph

explanation.surface: A cryptic question about what a skyward photograph produces.
explanation.walkthrough: A photo taken of the sky is literally an 'up shot'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the final outcome or consequence of something.

clue.text: Place of eternal punishment, unending for each abettor?

indicators.note: the word for that place loses its last letter

parts.note: hell is where the damned are punished forever
per means for each, as in 'per person'

explanation.surface: A grim warning that hell, for every accomplice, has no end.
explanation.definitionFit: An abettor assists another, typically in wrongdoing, so is an assistant or aide.

clue.text: Fuel sometimes supplied in bottles supporting sheet of glass?

parts.note: pro means in favour of, supporting a cause
a pane is a sheet of glass in a window

explanation.surface: A gas cylinder appears to be holding up a glass panel.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a hydrocarbon gas sold in pressurised cylinders for camping stoves and heaters.

clue.text: Garment maker alternatively extending part hanging at back of coat

indicators.note: the word for 'alternatively' is added onto the end of the coat part, lengthening it

parts.words: part hanging at back of coat
parts.note: the tail of a coat hangs down behind, as in tailcoat
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A dressmaker offers, as an option, to lengthen the back of a coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailor makes and alters clothes, especially suits and coats, to measure.

clue.text: Somehow salvages desert city

indicators.note: somehow suggests an unknown way of arranging, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone manages to rescue a city in the desert.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Nevada gambling capital was built in the Mojave Desert.

clue.text: Clever sting

definitions.meaning: to hurt with a sharp burning pain

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: bright and quick-witted, and to feel a sharp burning hurt, as a cut does when disinfected.

clue.text: Move on the subject of bloodshed

parts.note: to go is to move or travel
re means concerning, as in a business letter

explanation.surface: A motion is tabled about violence.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: spilt blood, especially from violence, as in a gory film.

clue.text: Choice of mild anaesthetic initially prolonged unconsciousness

indicators.note: the first letters of the four words before it are taken

explanation.surface: A patient chooses a gentle anaesthetic and ends up out cold for a long time.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep, lasting state of unconsciousness from which a patient cannot be woken.

clue.text: Stone added to display rack

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, a British unit of weight of 14 pounds
and joins things, adding one to another

explanation.surface: A stone is put onto a shelf for showing goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a frame or support on which items are shown, as in a market stall or hat holder.

clue.text: Lad tore ragged, stretchy costume

indicators.note: something ragged is torn and messed up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boy rips a garment until it is in tatters.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-fitting one-piece garment worn by dancers and gymnasts, made of elastic fabric.

clue.text: Knot with large wave — it should produce an outright winner

definitions.text: it should produce an outright winner

parts.note: a tie is a knot, as in tying a rope
a breaker is a large wave that crashes on the shore

explanation.surface: A sailor ties a knot as a huge wave rolls in.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: in tennis, an extra game played at six-all to decide a set when scores are level.
